title: Embeddings & Rerank Gateway — reconcile iterator semantics, retry hints, and legacy error translation
creator: Ayesha Malik
description: Problem: Legacy clients and a growing set of downstream services expect subtly different pagination and error semantics from our embeddings/rerank endpoints. Some clients rely on stable cursor envelopes, others expect Link headers and idempotent next/tombstone handling; meanwhile transient model-side failures are being surfaced inconsistently (sometimes 4xx, sometimes 5xx) which complicates client retry logic. This ticket proposes a compatibility gateway that normalizes iterator semantics, harmonizes HTTP error mapping and exposes explicit retry hints so both modern and legacy clients receive predictable behavior. The goal is parity across hosted/dedicated/private modes with a migration path that minimizes churn for integrations.
proposal: Introduce an embeddings-rerank compatibility gateway (sidecar/edge) that transforms our native responses into a stable, backwards-compatible envelope for legacy clients and a modern envelope for new clients based on Accept/Version headers.

Standardize cursor semantics: canonical cursor field 'next_cursor' (opaque base64), stable ordering guarantees per-request (document order + score tiebreaker), and explicit 'tombstone' markers when results were removed/deprecated.
Unify pagination transport: always include Link headers for page navigation (rel=next, rel=prev) where applicable, and include a Cursor response body field for clients that prefer body cursors.

Define an HTTP error mapping table: map internal transient model / infra errors -> 502/503 with Retry-After and machine-readable 'retry_hint' in JSON; map client errors (bad input, invalid model id) -> 400/422; map deprecations/invalid cursor -> 410 with clear 'migration_instructions' link.

Emit machine-readable retry hints: {"kind": "backoff", "min_ms": 100, "max_ms": 2000, "strategy": "exponential"} as string-encoded JSON in header X-Redwood-Retry-Hint and mirrored in body for compatibility.

Introduce idempotency token handling for paginated requests: allow clients to supply 'Idempotency-Key' to avoid duplicate work across retries; record token usage in audit logs and link to cost reconciliation dashboards.

Feature-flag rollout: gateway behind a feature flag per-region; start with passive transformation mode (no client-visible change) then active normalization for opt-in customers, followed by global opt-in after 2-week observation.
Provide an automated migration tool (CLI + SDK helper) that can translate legacy client paging calls into the new unified contract for customers with large fleets.
Add metrics and dashboards: per-client mismatch rate, cursor-invalidation events, retry-hint adherence, and percent of errors mapped by category.
Coordinate with SDK teams to expose client-friendly helpers (nextCursor(), shouldRetry()) and update docs with explicit guidance and examples.
Deliver compatibility spec and OpenAPI snippets for both legacy and new contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility gateway implemented and deployed to staging region behind a feature flag.
Gateway consistently returns Link headers and next_cursor body field for paginated responses in normalized mode.
Error mapping table implemented; simulated model transient errors surface as 502/503 with Retry-After and X-Redwood-Retry-Hint header in >= 95% of replayed cases.
Legacy clients that opt into compatibility mode experience no behavioral regressions in paging semantics for a 2-week trial (tracked via canary metrics).
SDKs updated with helper methods and docs updated with migration guide and examples.
Migration CLI can translate at least three common legacy client patterns and runs without data loss on sample datasets.
Relevant dashboards created and alerted: cursor-invalidations > 0.5% triggers triage, error-mapping drift > 3% triggers rollback.
Security review completed or waived (recorded in ticket).
migration_plan: Phase 1 (staging): Deploy gateway in passive mode - it mirrors requests and logs mismatches (2 days).
Phase 2 (canary): Enable active normalization for a small set of internal customers and SDK test-suite traffic (1 week). Collect metrics and adjust mappings.
Phase 3 (opt-in rollout): Expose API version header and allow customers to opt into normalized contract via console toggle or Accept-Version header (2 weeks).
Phase 4 (full roll): Flip feature flag region-by-region after no regressions found; provide a 30-day deprecation window for legacy behavior with opt-out available.
Phase 5 (sunset): After customer migration, run a final pass to remove legacy code paths and publish a post-mortem with lessons and rollout notes.
test_plan: Unit tests for cursor serialization/deserialization and ordering guarantees.
Integration tests: replay recorded production traffic against gateway to verify mappings and Link header / body cursor parity.
Chaos tests: inject transient model errors and verify gateway surfaces 502/503 + retry hint header consistently.
SDK tests: run end-to-end paging scenarios for legacy and new SDK helpers.
Load tests: validate gateway adds <3% p99 latency overhead at target QPS for dedicated and hosted deployments.
Manual QA checklist: cursor resume, partial page resume, de-dupe with Idempotency-Key, tombstone visibility, and invalid-cursor behavior.
notes: Trade-offs: A gateway maintains parity with minimal changes to the runtime but adds an operational hop and potential latency. We evaluated in-runtime normalization and rejected it because it increases coupling in the serving path.
Open questions: how to represent multi-model ranked sets when different models have differing TTLs for cached vectors? Consider adding per-item provenance in the envelope.
Fallback policy: Gateway will not synthesize results for missing pages; it will surface clear 410 with migration instructions for invalid cursors.
Cost considerations: audit logging of idempotency keys will increase storage for high-volume customers; include opt-out toggle in console.
